question: Can the useful torque training result be reproduced independently, while preserving R1 exactly when unarmed and refusing contact too late for a bumpless handoff?
changes: Inherit and call the entire R1 law. Use the R1 unload-capped carried fraction in a continuous convex combination with 0.45 before AND after release. Scale only the world-vertical Jacobian projection of position torque down to 0.20; never alter damping, detector, thresholds or grip. Arm between 120 and 20 ms before release with a positive known mass and public support >=0.05. Keep R1 on missing/late contact. Fixed 20 ms rise, 40 ms fade.
protocol: First verify synthetic late and absent contact, and full 6000-cycle no-payload R1 byte parity. Then compare four new normal pairs, including lighter payload, nuisance and vertical pickup offset. All four G4 gates, each cost <=1.05 matching R1, no new saturation, divergence, or false alarm; byte-identical before arming. If any group fails, do not open a held collision set, do not promote, retain utility as research-only. No detector tuning or truth-based compensation.
inputs: encoders, JTS, grip, public reference, known box and nominal robot only. No access to drive internals or detector alarms. Physical measurements after episode. No hardware or safety claim.
